setting: A short talk in an introductory psychology class about how habits form and how to change them.
narrator_intro: Listen to part of a talk in a psychology class.

talk.speaker: speaker1
talk.text: A habit is a behavior that becomes automatic after repeated practice in a stable context.

talk.speaker: speaker1
talk.text: Researchers often describe a simple loop: cue, routine, and reward.

talk.speaker: speaker1
talk.text: The cue is a trigger—time of day, a place, or a feeling—that starts the behavior.

talk.speaker: speaker1
talk.text: The routine is the action itself, and the reward is whatever makes your brain want to repeat it.

talk.speaker: speaker1
talk.text: Once a habit is strong, you may start the routine with little conscious planning.

talk.speaker: speaker1
talk.text: That efficiency saves mental energy, but it also makes unhealthy habits hard to break.

talk.speaker: speaker1
talk.text: One evidence-based strategy is to keep the same cue and reward while swapping in a better routine.

talk.speaker: speaker1
talk.text: For example, if stress cues afternoon snacking, you might replace chips with a short walk that still reduces tension.

talk.speaker: speaker1
talk.text: Changing the environment—removing the cue—also helps more than relying on willpower alone.

talk.speaker: speaker1
talk.text: Next class we’ll look at experiments on how long new habits typically take to stabilize.

narrator_outro: Now get ready to answer the questions.

questions.correctAnswer: How habits form and one way to change them

questions.narrator_text: According to the professor, what are the three parts of the habit loop?
questions.explanation: She describes the loop as cue, routine, and reward.

questions.narrator_text: What strategy does she recommend for changing a habit?

options.text: Keep the same cue and reward but swap in a better routine
Ignore cues and never seek any reward
Only use willpower and never change the environment
Change every habit at the same time with no plan

questions.correctAnswer: Keep the same cue and reward but swap in a better routine

options.text: They always require careful planning every time
